FLASHCARD SET · AGES 3–4 YEARS

Shape Flashcards for Preschoolers

Twelve shape cards, from the everyday circle to the eight-sided octagon. One big friendly shape per card, its name to read together, and a shape hunt to try — pick a card, name it and go find it in your house.

These cards belong to Preschool · Age 3 on the Kiddo School learning path.

THE CARDS

Every card in the set.

Every card is right here on one page: the picture and short, practical notes for grown-ups — what it is for, how to use it, how to print it. Read every card right here.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Two shapes are a fine first day

    Circle and star, or circle and heart — start with the two your child will spot most around the house. Naming two shapes well beats rushing through twelve.

  2. 02

    Hunt first, flashcards second

    Shape names stick when they are attached to real things. Find a plate-circle or a door-rectangle first, then show the card — the card confirms what your child already discovered.

  3. 03

    Say the shape, then trace it

    Name the shape and draw it in the air with one big finger movement. Round for circle, three sharp turns for triangle — the hand helps the word land.

  4. 04

    Let the shapes live somewhere

    Tape today’s shape near a real example: the circle card by the clock, the heart card on the family noticeboard. Passing them together all day is quiet, powerful practice.

      FLASHCARD · SHAPES & PATTERNS · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Circle Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The circle is the perfect first shape: no corners, no sides, just round and round. Wheels, plates, clocks, cookies — your home is full of them, which means your child can meet this card’s shape fifty times before lunch.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this shape card does

      Gives a real name to the shape of lids, buttons and breakfast plates.

      Shape hunt

      Drawer dive: fish out every round lid you can find and stack the winners.

      What kids learn from it

      Spotting and naming curves — the start of telling shapes apart.

      How to print it

      Print it at teatime size and prop it against the bread bin.

      Tip for today

      Hunt low — the best circles live at knee height on pans.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Circle lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SHAPES & PATTERNS · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Square Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Four sides, four corners, all the same length — the square is the shape of crackers, windows and sticky notes. It is usually the second shape children name, right after circle, because corners are so easy to count on it.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this shape card does

      Explains why some things stack and others slide — four steady sides.

      Shape hunt

      Shape hunt through the sofa cushions; who finds the flattest square wins bragging rights.

      What kids learn from it

      Same-length sides make a shape steady enough to build with.

      How to print it

      A pair of copies works: one for the wall, one for matching.

      Tip for today

      Let them win the last find; a victorious hunter hunts again tomorrow.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Square lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SHAPES & PATTERNS · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Triangle Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Three sides, three corners, pointy and proud. Triangles are roofs, pizza slices and mountains in children’s drawings — and the word itself is a mouthful that three-year-olds love to get right.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this shape card does

      Describes the shape that points back — three sides, three corners, all business.

      Shape hunt

      Comb the toy shelf for anything with three sides; hats and wedges count double.

      What kids learn from it

      Counting a shape's parts — sides and corners — without losing your place.

      How to print it

      Print at A4 and pin it above the craft table.

      Tip for today

      Fold a napkin corner to corner; hand over the triangle you made.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Triangle lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SHAPES & PATTERNS · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Rectangle Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A square’s long cousin: four sides, four corners, stretched out wide. Doors, books, tables and screens are rectangles, so this is the shape your child has been touching all day without knowing its name.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this shape card does

      Names the stretched-out shape your child opens, closes and climbs over all day.

      Shape hunt

      Tour the kitchen for rectangles and finish at the biggest one — the fridge door.

      What kids learn from it

      Telling long sides from short ones — comparing two things on one shape.

      How to print it

      A5 taped to the fridge door suits this one nicely.

      Tip for today

      Trace long side, short side, long side with one slow finger.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Rectangle lesson on the Learning Path.

      Oval Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The oval is a circle that has been gently stretched — egg-shaped, balloon-shaped, relaxed. It often arrives hand-in-hand with the circle in a child’s mind, as the shape that is “almost round but not quite”.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this shape card does

      Covers the in-between shape — nearly round, slightly stretchy, hard to pin down.

      Shape hunt

      Scan the bathroom shelf for ovals; soap bars and sponges qualify.

      What kids learn from it

      Seeing how one small change makes a brand-new shape.

      How to print it

      Print it beside the circle card so the two can argue.

      Tip for today

      Ask which shape would make a better wheel — expect strong opinions.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Oval lesson on the Learning Path.

      Star Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Five points, sparkly reputation, instant favourite. The star may be the shape your child already knows best — stickers, drawings, night-sky books — which makes it the confidence-booster of this set.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this shape card does

      Adds some sparkle to the pile: five points, easy to spot, fun to draw.

      Shape hunt

      Sweep the bookshelf for hidden stars — spines, covers, pajama prints.

      What kids learn from it

      Careful counting to five on a shape that rewards getting it right.

      How to print it

      Crayons ready — this shape begs to be traced and coloured.

      Tip for today

      Four points or seven, a proud shape is still a star.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Star lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SHAPES & PATTERNS · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Heart Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The shape of love, drawings and handmade cards. Most three-year-olds meet the heart before any other shape because it comes attached to affection — and this card keeps that feeling: soft, warm and simple.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this shape card does

      Puts a name tag on the shape your child already draws daily.

      Shape hunt

      Check packaging, clothes labels and yesterday's drawings for hearts.

      What kids learn from it

      Symmetry by feel: two bumps on top, one point below, always.

      How to print it

      Pink paper if the cupboard allows; white works just as well.

      Tip for today

      Mail one to a grandparent; shapes travel well in envelopes.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Heart lesson on the Learning Path.

      Diamond Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A square standing on its corner — pointy at the top, pointy at the bottom, like a kite climbing the wind. Preschoolers often meet this shape as the gem in a treasure chest or the pattern on socks.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this shape card does

      Points out the fancy shape hiding in fences, wrapping paper and Granny's earrings.

      Shape hunt

      Shape hunt on the way home: railings, fence panels, Nan's argyle socks.

      What kids learn from it

      Recognising one shape in lots of places, even as a pattern.

      How to print it

      Pocket-sized at A5, for hunts that leave the house.

      Tip for today

      Patterned clothes are full of diamonds; the laundry basket is a quarry.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Diamond lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SHAPES & PATTERNS · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Crescent Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The moon shape: a circle with a sleepy bite taken out of it. Bananas curve this way, moons in storybooks shine this way, and the word crescent is a lovely new sound for little mouths to try.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this shape card does

      Gives the moon shape a proper name, shoutable from any bedroom window.

      Shape hunt

      Inspect tonight's sky from the window; if cloudy, draw your own moon.

      What kids learn from it

      Shapes that curve one way, then the other — trickier than they look.

      How to print it

      Stick it low on the bedroom wall, at reaching height.

      Tip for today

      Point it out at bedtime and let the day end looking upward.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Crescent lesson on the Learning Path.

      Pentagon Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Five straight sides, five corners — the biggest shape most three-year-olds have ever met. The word is a glorious mouthful, and getting “pentagon” out loud is half the fun and half the achievement.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this shape card does

      Brings a five-sided wonder and a word longer than most biscuits are wide.

      Shape hunt

      Search the sports kit and front room for anything five-sided; expect a short list.

      What kids learn from it

      A long word and the glow of pronouncing it correctly.

      How to print it

      Card stock, please — this one deserves to survive the decade.

      Tip for today

      Rarer than the others, so enjoy a slow hunt; scarcity builds suspense.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Pentagon lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SHAPES & PATTERNS · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Hexagon Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Six sides, six corners — the bee’s favourite shape. Honeycombs are built from hexagons because they fit together perfectly, and that one fact turns this card into a story your child may retell for weeks.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this shape card does

      Delivers six sides and a shape that fits its neighbours perfectly.

      Shape hunt

      Raid the toy boxes and tool drawer for six-sided bits; report all finds.

      What kids learn from it

      Counting to six on one shape, with corners to prove it.

      How to print it

      Any paper works; cut spares into tiles for fitting games.

      Tip for today

      Fit two edge to edge and admire the snug little join.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Hexagon lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SHAPES & PATTERNS · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Octagon Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Eight sides — and one very famous job. The stop sign is an octagon, which makes this the shape with the best real-world game attached: every walk can become an octagon hunt.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this shape card does

      Completes the class with eight sides and a name worth announcing.

      Shape hunt

      Hunt the house for octagons — they hide well, so grade on effort.

      What kids learn from it

      Eight corners, all present and correct — counting with confidence.

      How to print it

      A4, laminated, so it can referee games for years.

      Tip for today

      Draw one from memory and count the sides; laughs guaranteed.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Octagon lesson on the Learning Path.
